title: Effects of Passiflora edulis Leaf Extract on Lipid Accumulation in HepG2 Cells: In Vitro Evidence and Molecular Docking Analysis Involving PPARalpha and SREBP-1.
authors: Aguillon Osma, Johanny; Leon Villarreal, John Sebastian; Loango Chamorro, Nelsy
one_liner_zh: 该文研究西番莲叶提取物对HepG2细胞脂质积累的抑制，并用分子对接评估其与PPARalpha和SREBP-1转录因子的结合，虽涉及转录因子-小分子对接，但对象非蛋白质-DNA互作，方法仅简单对接，与TF-DNA结合机制课题关联较弱。
abstract: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is characterized by excessive hepatic lipid accumulation and represents a major global health concern. Passiflora edulis contains numerous phytochemicals associated with diverse biological activities, including hepatoprotective and hypolipidemic effects. This study evaluated the effects of the ethanolic extract of P. edulis leaves on lipid accumulation in a cellular model of NAFLD, as well as its potential effect on transcriptional factors involved in lipid metabolism. HepG2 cells were exposed to steatogenic conditions and treated with the extract at non-cytotoxic concentrations, quantifying intracellular and extracellular triglycerides and cholesterol levels. Additionally, molecular docking analyses were performed to evaluate the interaction of reported P. edulis phytochemicals with PPARalpha and SREBP-1. The results revealed a significant reduction in intracellular lipid content compared to untreated cells, while molecular docking predicted favorable binding interactions between the bioactive compounds in the extract, with higher predicted affinity for PPARalpha (agonist-like interaction) than for SREBP-1c (antagonist-like interaction). These findings suggest that compounds from P. edulis leaves reduce lipid accumulation in liver cells and provide preliminary evidence supporting possible interactions with lipid-regulating transcription factors.
abstract_zh: 非酒精性脂肪性肝病（NAFLD）以肝脏脂质过度蓄积为特征，是全球重大健康问题。西番莲（Passiflora edulis）含有多种植物化学物质，具有多种生物活性，包括保肝和降脂作用。本研究评估了西番莲叶片乙醇提取物对NAFLD细胞模型中脂质蓄积的影响，及其对参与脂质代谢的转录因子的潜在作用。将HepG2细胞置于致脂肪变性条件下，并以非细胞毒性浓度处理提取物，定量检测细胞内和细胞外甘油三酯及胆固醇水平。此外，进行了分子对接分析，以评估已报道的西番莲植物化学物质与PPARalpha和SREBP-1的相互作用。结果显示，与未处理细胞相比，细胞内脂质含量显著降低，而分子对接预测提取物中的生物活性化合物具有有利的结合相互作用，对PPARalpha（激动剂样相互作用）的预测亲和力高于对SREBP-1c（拮抗剂样相互作用）。这些发现表明，西番莲叶片中的化合物可减少肝细胞中的脂质蓄积，并提供了支持其可能与脂质调节转录因子相互作用的初步证据。
